comparator.name: International Development Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official handbook defines 180 EC: 114 EC of common study, a 36-EC specialisation and 30 EC of open electives. Sociology of Development is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break from the three equally formal specialisations.

components.name: Global Challenges and Communication in a Changing World
Research Methods in the Social Sciences
Critical Perspectives on Agricultural and Rural Development
Economics Evolving: A History of Ideas of Development and Growth
Economic and Sociological Analysis of Rural Livelihoods
Methods, Techniques and Data Analysis for Field Research
Globalization and Sustainability of Food Production and Consumption
The Sociology of Farming and Rural Life
Planetary Development: Sociological and Anthropological Perspectives
Open electives and minor
components.note: Genuine open elective space; no minor or course package is invented.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum combines sociology, political science, economics, international law, history, communication and mixed research methods around inequality, justice and global development.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Thirteen courses differ in each direction from CHS and twenty from Earth and Sustainability. Political economy, legal institutions, human rights and international security become the organising core.

assessedInterests.studentInterest: why hunger persists despite sufficient food
building fairer and more inclusive societies
understanding development through sociology, economics and politics
investigating why prosperity is distributed unequally
asking why hunger exists when the world produces enough food
conducting development field research in England, Ireland or the Netherlands
analysing an NGO programme on land rights
comparing economic and sociological explanations of poverty
examining the environmental effects of a development policy
working for an NGO such as UNICEF or Oxfam Novib
communication and fundraising for development organisations
working for a foreign-affairs ministry or embassy
working for the European Union, WTO or FAO
research or teaching at a university or NGO

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The generic target has three equally formal 36-EC specialisations: Sociology of Development, Economics of Development, and Politics and Communication in Development. None is identified as the general route, so the first current handbook specialisation is selected neutrally and independently of UCR fit.

candidateAssessments.organisingLogic: The explicitly supplied candidate direction is “Development economics & global political economy”; its interest-row basis and disposition remain explicit in interestSelection.
candidateAssessments.assessment: The academic decision includes this candidate as ucr-2.

candidateAssessments.organisingLogic: The explicitly supplied candidate direction is “Development sociology, culture & communication”; its interest-row basis and disposition remain explicit in interestSelection.
candidateAssessments.assessment: The academic decision includes this candidate as ucr-3.

notes.text: WUR provides a dedicated development-studies sequence with rural livelihoods, agricultural development, specialised field research and a development thesis. UCR can combine substantial sociology, economics, politics, law, history and communication, but does not reproduce the same field-based or rural-development sequence course for course.
